To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the classification of keyphrase in scientific publications is possible using a combination of WordNet and word embedding features, and that the ScienceIE collection contains some errors that need to be addressed in future work.
• WordNet-based methods are effective in the classification of key concepts, but not in the classification of task-related concepts; • Word embeddings are effective in all three types of concepts.
• The best performing system for the classification of scientific keyphrases according the the ScienceIE classification is a system based on word embeddings and WordNet features.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to automatic keyphrase generation.
the automatic classification of the main concepts that are used to describe the research activities in scientific publications.
the classification of key phrases in the context of scientific publications, according to the Science IE task at SemEval 2017.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the classification of keyphrase types into process, material and task is a useful one for the analysis of keyphrases.
the proposed approach is a good one, but the task is not yet mature and needs more work.

the ScienceIE classification is a promising direction to take in the field of keyphrase extraction, and that the proposed method is able to outperform the state-of-the-art, although the collection is still far from ideal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to classify keyphrases according the epistemological classification suggested by the ScienceIE task, using WordNet-based and word embeddings features.
we have proposed a new method for the classification and ranking of keyphrases, based on the ScienceIE epistemological classification.
we have shown that the ScienceIE task is not a trivial one, but that the classification is possible using the right tools.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ScienceIE task, while interesting, is still in its infancy. It would require a more robust annotation scheme to become a reliable benchmark for keyphrase classification.
the task of classifying keyphrases according a ScienceIE classification is feasible and that the best results can be obtained using WordNet and embeddings derived features.
, despite the fact that the task is not trivial, it is feasible with current NLP technology.
